mainTopic: The greatness of מילה, wholehearted trust in ה׳, and teachings about אברהם
overview: This עמוד finishes the story of משה at the lodging place, where he was punished for dealing with the lodging before circumcising his son. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the danger was really aimed at the baby. רבי יהודה בר ביזנא describes how the angels אף and חימה swallowed משה until צפורה did the מילה. The גמרא then discusses whether משה later killed חימה. Next comes a ברייתא praising מילה: it made אברהם 'תמים', it equals all the מצוות, and it holds up heaven and earth. רבי אליעזר says that last praise belongs to תורה. Teachings follow about אברהם's fear and reassurance, 'אין מזל לישראל', the reward for being תמים, and the harm of chasing omens. The גמרא then gives three opinions on why אברהם's children were enslaved in מצרים. It ends with number-value teachings about אליעזר and about אברהם recognizing his Creator at age three, and begins a statement of רמי בר אבא that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: משה was punished for dealing with the lodging first
steps.stepSummary: The reason משה was punished is that he got busy with arranging his lodging before doing the מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he busied himself with the lodging first, as it says: "And it was on the way, at the lodging place."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer that started just before this section: why was משה punished on the way to Egypt? The answer is that he took care of his lodging before circumcising his son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier view held that משה had a good reason to delay the מילה, because traveling right after a מילה could be dangerous for the baby. Even so, once he arrived at the lodging place he should have done the מילה right away. Instead he dealt with the lodging first. The proof comes from the words "at the lodging place" in the פסוק, which show that the danger came at exactly that point.

keyTerms.meaning: Lodging place, an inn
He busied himself with, he got occupied with
First, before anything else

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying משה ignored the מצוה. The point is that he delayed it, even for a short time, at a moment when he could already have done it.

phrases.english: Because he busied himself with the lodging first,
phrases.notes: This finishes an answer from just before this section, to the question of why משה was punished.

phrases.english: as it says: "And it was on the way, at the lodging place."
phrases.notes: שמות 4:24

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the question of why משה was punished, which was asked just before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why was משה punished, if delaying the מילה because of travel was justified?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because at the lodging place he took care of the lodging before doing the מילה.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the danger was aimed at the baby
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the שטן wanted to kill the uncircumcised baby, not משה, and proves it from the word "חתן".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: The שטן did not want to kill משה our teacher, but that baby, as it says: "For you are a bridegroom of blood to me." Go and see: who is called a 'bridegroom'? You must say it is the baby.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion is brought. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the one in danger was the baby, not משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not clearly say who was attacked. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל uses צפורה's words, "you are a חתן דמים to me", to decide. The one who just entered the covenant through the blood of מילה is the baby, so the baby is the 'חתן', the one who was in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: The Satan, the accusing angel
A baby, a young child
A 'bridegroom of blood', a term צפורה used during the מילה
Go out and see, meaning 'think about it'
You must say, meaning this is the only possible answer

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how serious it is to leave a child without מילה. The danger fell on the baby himself.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ בִּקֵּשׁ שָׂטָן לַהֲרוֹג,
phrases.english: It was not Moshe our teacher that the Satan wanted to kill,
but rather that baby,
phrases.notes: He means משה's son, who had not yet had his מילה.

phrases.english: as it says: "For you are a bridegroom of blood to me."
phrases.notes: שמות 4:25

phrases.english: Go out and see: who is called a 'bridegroom'?
You must say: this is the baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: לֹא לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ בִּקֵּשׁ שָׂטָן לַהֲרוֹג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading: the target was the baby, not משה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שטן sought to kill the uncircumcised baby, as shown by the word 'חתן' in the פסוק.

steps.title: The angels אף and חימה swallowed משה until the מילה was done
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר ביזנא teaches that when משה was slow about the מילה, the angels אף and חימה swallowed him up to his legs, and they let go as soon as צפורה did the מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בר ביזנא taught: When משה our teacher was slow about the מילה, 'Anger' and 'Wrath' came and swallowed him, and left nothing of him except his legs. Immediately "צפורה took a flint and cut off her son's foreskin," and immediately "He let him go."
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching describes what happened to משה. Two destructive angels named אף and חימה swallowed him, and the moment the מילה was done, they released him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching goes back to the view that משה himself was in danger. The word 'immediately' appears twice to show a direct cause and effect: the מילה was done, and right away משה was saved. That shows the power of the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Was lax, slow, or negligent about something
'Anger' and 'Wrath', here the names of two destructive angels
They swallowed him
A flint, a sharp stone
And He let go, He released

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda bar Bizna taught:

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁנִּתְרַשֵּׁל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ מִן הַמִּילָה,
phrases.english: At the time that Moshe our teacher was slow about the circumcision,
'Anger' and 'Wrath' came and swallowed him,
phrases.notes: These are two destructive angels, named Anger and Wrath.

phrases.english: and they left nothing of him except his legs.
Immediately, "Tzippora took a flint
and cut off her son's foreskin,"
phrases.notes: שמות 4:25

phrases.english: immediately, "He let him go."
phrases.notes: שמות 4:26

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new teaching describing the danger to משה and his rescue through the מילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Delaying the מילה brought the angels אף and חימה upon משה, and doing the מילה saved him right away.

steps.title: משה wanted to kill the angels
steps.stepSummary: After he was saved, משה wanted to kill אף and חימה, which is hinted at in a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that moment משה our teacher wanted to kill them, as it says: "Let go of anger and abandon wrath."
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. After he was released, משה wanted to kill the two angels, and a פסוק is brought as a hint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים names both אף and חימה. Reading these words as the names of the angels, the teaching hears in it משה's wish to get rid of them both.

keyTerms.meaning: To kill them
Let go of, cease from

phrases.aramaic: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה בִּיקֵּשׁ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לְהוֹרְגָן,
phrases.english: At that moment, Moshe our teacher wanted to kill them,
as it says: "Let go of anger and abandon wrath."
phrases.notes: תהלים 37:8

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה בִּיקֵּשׁ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לְהוֹרְגָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רבי יהודה בר ביזנא: what משה did after he was saved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה wanted to kill אף and חימה.

steps.title: Some say משה actually killed חימה
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion says משה did kill the angel חימה, based on the פסוק "חמה אין לי".
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: He killed 'Wrath', as it says: "I have no wrath."
steps.whatsHappening: A different opinion goes further. משה did not only want to kill, he actually killed חימה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a פסוק in ישעיהו that says there is no 'חמה'. It is read as saying that חימה no longer exists, because it was killed.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say, introducing another opinion
He killed him

phrases.english: And some say: he killed 'Wrath',
as it says: "I have no wrath."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 27:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes further than the previous step: חימה was not just threatened but actually killed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה killed the angel חימה.

steps.title: Challenge: משה later says he feared חימה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how חימה could have been killed, if much later משה says he was afraid of 'the anger and the wrath'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: "For I was afraid of the anger and the wrath"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that חימה was killed, using a פסוק from משה's own words years later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ספר דברים, long after the event at the lodging place, משה says he was afraid of 'the anger and the wrath'. If חימה had already been killed, there would be nothing left to fear. So the 'יש אומרים' seems to contradict this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it not written? An opening for a challenge from a פסוק
I was afraid

phrases.english: But it is written: "For I was afraid of the anger and the wrath"!
phrases.notes: דברים 9:19. משה said this many years after the lodging place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim in step 5 that חימה was killed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'יש אומרים' that משה killed חימה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה later feared חימה, so חימה must still have existed.

steps.title: Answer: there were two angels named חימה
steps.stepSummary: There were two separate angels called חימה. משה killed one, and the other remained.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were two 'Wraths'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: there were two angels called חימה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once there are two angels with that name, both פסוקים can be true. משה killed one חימה, and later he feared the other one.

keyTerms.meaning: Two
There were

phrases.english: There were two 'Wraths'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: two separate entities share the same name.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There was only one חימה, so if it was killed, משה could not fear it later.
steps.terutzMaskana: One חימה was killed, and a second חימה remained for משה to fear later.

steps.title: Second answer: the army of חימה remained
steps.stepSummary: Another answer is that משה killed חימה itself, but its army stayed, and that is what he feared later.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: the army of 'Wrath'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. What משה feared later was חימה's army, not חימה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is only one angel called חימה, and it was killed. But its troops survived, and the later פסוק refers to them. Either answer saves the view that משה killed חימה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say, introducing a second answer
An army or troop

steps.whatToRemember: Delaying מילה even briefly brought great danger, and doing it saved משה or his son at once. The view that משה killed חימה survives the challenge from דברים, either because there were two angels called חימה or because חימה's army remained.

phrases.english: And if you want, say: the army of 'Wrath'.
phrases.notes: He means משה killed חימה itself, but later he feared the troops it left behind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the later פסוק refers to the army, not the angel itself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'חמה' that משה feared later was the angel חימה itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה feared חימה's army, which survived after חימה was killed.

steps.title: Circumcision made אברהם complete
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי: מילה is great, because even אברהם אבינו, who did so many מצוות, was only called 'תמים' because of מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: רבי says: מילה is great. No one was as busy with מצוות as אברהם אבינו, and still he was called 'complete' only because of מילה. The פסוק says 'Walk before Me and be complete,' and right after that it says 'And I will place My covenant between Me and you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי praises מילה. He proves it from the fact that אברהם became 'תמים' only through מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם had already done countless מצוות, yet the תורה tells him to 'become complete' only now. The very next פסוק talks about the ברית, which is מילה. So it was מילה, and not his other מצוות, that made him 'תמים'.

keyTerms.meaning: Great is the מצוה of circumcision
Complete, whole, without any missing part
Covenant; here it means the covenant of מילה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first of three praises of מילה. The two פסוקים here come back again in רב's story in step 13.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא, often just called 'רבי'.

phrases.english: Great is circumcision,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לָךְ מִי שֶׁנִּתְעַסֵּק בְּמִצְוֹת כְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ,
phrases.english: for there is no one who busied himself with מצוות like Avraham our father,
and yet he was not called 'complete'
except because of circumcision,
as it says: "Walk before Me and be complete,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 17:1

phrases.english: and it is written: "And I will place My covenant between Me and you."
phrases.notes: בראשית 17:2. This 'covenant' is the מצוה of מילה, which is given to אברהם right here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of משה and the angels and opens a new set of teachings praising מילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה is great, because only through it was אברהם called 'תמים'.

steps.title: Circumcision equals all the מצוות
steps.stepSummary: A second reason: מילה is as weighty as all the מצוות of the תורה together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: מילה is great, because it is equal to all the מצוות in the תורה, as it says: 'For according to these words, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second, separate reason why מילה is great: it weighs as much as all the other מצוות put together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק goes on to say 'I have made a covenant with you.' The word 'covenant' hints at מילה, and it is linked to 'these words', meaning the whole תורה. So מילה stands against everything in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation; a new, separate reason
Equal in weight to
'Etc.', meaning the rest of the פסוק is assumed

phrases.english: Another explanation: Great is circumcision,
for it is equal to all the מצוות in the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי עַל פִּי הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: as it says: "For according to these words, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות 34:27. The rest of the פסוק says 'I have made a covenant with you.' That word 'covenant' is the hint to מילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: גְּדוֹלָה מִילָה, שֶׁשְּׁקוּלָה כְּנֶגֶד כׇּל הַמִּצְוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent reason for the greatness of מילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה is equal to all the מצוות of the תורה.

steps.title: Heaven and earth exist because of circumcision
steps.stepSummary: A third reason: without מילה, heaven and earth would not have lasted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: מילה is great, because if not for מילה, heaven and earth would not have lasted, as it says: 'If not for My covenant day and night, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third reason: the whole world stays in place because of מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיהו says that if not for 'My covenant day and night', God would not have set up the laws of heaven and earth. This 'דבר אחר' of the ברייתא reads that 'covenant day and night' as מילה, which is on a person's body all day and all night.

keyTerms.meaning: If not for; were it not for
Would have lasted, stayed in place
Day and night

phrases.english: Another explanation: Great is circumcision,
for were it not for circumcision
heaven and earth would not have lasted,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אִם לֹא בְּרִיתִי יוֹמָם וָלָיְלָה וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: as it says: "If not for My covenant day and night, etc."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 33:25. The 'covenant day and night' is מילה, since it stays on the body all the time.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: גְּדוֹלָה מִילָה, שֶׁאִילְמָלֵא מִילָה לֹא נִתְקַיְּימוּ שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third reason for the greatness of מילה, using a פסוק that the next step will show is read differently by רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven and earth exist because of מילה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר reads the same verse as being about Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי אליעזר disagrees: he says the same פסוק teaches that heaven and earth exist because of תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר said: תורה is great, because if not for תורה, heaven and earth would not have lasted, as it says: 'If not for My covenant day and night, I would not have set the laws of heaven and earth, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא comments that the last teaching argues with רבי אליעזר, who reads the very same פסוק as talking about תורה, not מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions use the same פסוק, and both agree that some 'covenant day and night' keeps the world going. They argue only about what that covenant is. For the ברייתא's 'דבר אחר' it is מילה; for רבי אליעזר it is תורה, which is learned day and night.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees; it argues with
Great is the תורה
The fixed laws of heaven and earth (how nature runs)

steps.confusionAlert: The two opinions do not argue about whether a 'covenant' holds up the world. They argue only about which covenant the פסוק means: מילה or תורה.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Eliezer,
for Rabbi Eliezer said:
Great is the Torah,
for were it not for Torah
heaven and earth would not have lasted,
as it says: "If not for My covenant day and night,

phrases.aramaic: חֻקּוֹת שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ לֹא שָׂמְתִּי וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: I would not have set the laws of heaven and earth, etc."
phrases.notes: For רבי אליעזר, 'day and night' points to תורה, which we are told to learn day and night (יהושע 1:8).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the third reason in step 11 argues with רבי אליעזר's reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, heaven and earth exist because of תורה, and the 'covenant day and night' is the תורה.

steps.title: אברהם trembles and is then reassured
steps.stepSummary: רב tells that when אברהם was told 'be complete', he was scared he had some flaw. When he heard about the ברית of מילה, he calmed down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: When הקדוש ברוך הוא told אברהם אבינו 'Walk before Me and be complete', trembling took hold of him. He said: 'Maybe there is something disgraceful in me.' Once God told him 'And I will place My covenant between Me and you', his mind was put at ease.
steps.whatsHappening: רב tells a story built on the same two פסוקים from step 9. אברהם was afraid he was missing something, and he relaxed once he heard that the missing piece was מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being told to 'become complete' made אברהם think he had some hidden sin or flaw. The next פסוק showed him that what he lacked was only the מצוה of מילה, which he was about to receive. This fits רבי's teaching in step 9 that מילה is what made אברהם 'תמים'.

keyTerms.meaning: Trembling took hold of him
Something disgraceful or shameful
His mind was cooled; he calmed down

steps.whatToRemember: מילה is praised in three ways: it made אברהם 'תמים', it equals all the מצוות, and it holds up heaven and earth (רבי אליעזר says that last one is about תורה). רב's story shows that the 'completeness' אברהם lacked was only מילה.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
phrases.english: At the time that the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Avraham our father:
"Walk before Me and be complete,"
trembling took hold of him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: שֶׁמָּא יֵשׁ בִּי דָּבָר מְגוּנֶּה.
phrases.english: He said: Perhaps there is something disgraceful in me.
Once He said to him:
"And I will place My covenant between Me and you,"
his mind was put at ease.
phrases.notes: Literally, 'his mind cooled down.' He saw that what he was missing was only מילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the two פסוקים from step 9 and tells the story behind them, showing that מילה is what made אברהם complete.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אברהם feared he had a flaw when told to be 'תמים', and was reassured when he learned that what he lacked was the ברית of מילה.

steps.title: אברהם told to leave his stargazing: Israel is above the stars
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק 'He brought him outside,' אברהם says his מזל shows only one son. הקדוש ברוך הוא tells him to leave astrology, because אין מזל לישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And He brought him outside.' אברהם said before Him: Master of the World, I looked at my star, and I am meant to have only one son. He answered: Step out of your stargazing. Israel is not ruled by the stars.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains a פסוק about אברהם. It teaches that the Jewish people are not controlled by the stars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם thought his future was fixed by his מזל. הקדוש ברוך הוא told him to 'go out' of that way of thinking. The word 'outside' in the פסוק is read as leaving the world of astrology behind.

keyTerms.meaning: A star or constellation, believed to decide a person's fate
Astrology, stargazing
Master of the World, a way of addressing הקדוש ברוך הוא

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous source for the idea 'אין מזל לישראל'. It also sets up the theme of the next steps: trusting הקדוש ברוך הוא wholeheartedly instead of signs and stars.

phrases.english: "And He brought him outside"
phrases.notes: בראשית 15:5

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the World,
I looked at my star
and I am meant to have only one son.
He said to him: Go out of your stargazing,
phrases.notes: 'Go out' plays on 'He brought him outside' from the פסוק.

phrases.english: Israel has no star (ruling its fate).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the stories about אברהם and his relationship with הקדוש ברוך הוא after the ברית מילה story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אין מזל לישראל: the Jewish people are not bound by astrology.

steps.title: Whoever is wholehearted with God is treated wholeheartedly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that if a person is wholehearted with הקדוש ברוך הוא, הקדוש ברוך הוא is wholehearted with him. He brings a פסוק from שמואל ב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Anyone who makes himself wholehearted, הקדוש ברוך הוא is wholehearted with him, as it says: 'With the devout You act devoutly, with the strong, wholehearted one You act wholeheartedly.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק adds a teaching about being תמים‎. ה׳ treats a person the same way that person treats Him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to אברהם being told 'be תמים' and to leaving the stars behind. Simple trust in הקדוש ברוך הוא brings the same simple, complete care from Him. The פסוק shows that ה׳ matches how a person acts.

keyTerms.meaning: Acts wholeheartedly, with simple and complete trust
A devout, pious person
Wholehearted, complete

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Anyone who makes himself wholehearted,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, acts wholeheartedly with him,
as it says: "With the devout You act devoutly,
with the strong, wholehearted one You act wholeheartedly."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 22:26

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק כׇּל הַמְתַמֵּים עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אברהם is told to leave stargazing, a general teaching is added about the reward for being wholehearted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever is תמים with הקדוש ברוך הוא is treated with the same wholeheartedness.

steps.title: Whoever is wholehearted has time on his side
steps.stepSummary: רבי הושעיא teaches that whoever is wholehearted succeeds. His proof is that right after אברהם is told to be תמים, he is promised many nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי הושעיא said: Anyone who makes himself wholehearted, the hour stands for him, as it says: 'Walk before Me and be wholehearted,' and it is written: 'And you will be the father of many nations.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי הושעיא gives another reward for being תמים: things will go well for him. He proves it from two nearby פסוקים about אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First פסוק: אברהם is told to be תמים. A few פסוקים later he is promised he will be 'father of many nations', far more than the one son his star showed. Being wholehearted brought him success.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the hour stands for him': the time works in his favor and he succeeds
And it is written, used to bring a second פסוק
A multitude of nations

phrases.english: Rabbi Hoshaya said:
Anyone who makes himself wholehearted,
the hour stands for him,
phrases.notes: He means that time is on his side and he succeeds.

phrases.english: as it says: "Walk before Me and be wholehearted,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 17:1

phrases.english: and it is written: "And you will be the father of many nations."
phrases.notes: בראשית 17:4

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא כׇּל הַמְתַמֵּים עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second אמורא adds another reward for being תמים, this time proven from אברהם's own story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever is תמים succeeds; time stands in his favor.

steps.title: Whoever looks for omens is hurt by omens
steps.stepSummary: רבי says that a person who looks for omens will be harmed by omens. He reads the word לא in a פסוק as if it were לו, 'to him'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: Anyone who looks for omens, the omen comes to him, as it says: 'For there is no omen in Jacob.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי teaches the opposite side of being תמים: someone who chases signs about the future will be hurt by them. He tries to prove it from a פסוק in בלעם's blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי reads 'כי לא נחש' as if it said 'לו נחש', 'the omen is to him.' That would mean the omen comes back against the person who uses it. The next step questions this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who looks for omens or signs to predict the future
An omen, a sign used for fortune-telling
As it says, used to bring a פסוק as proof

phrases.english: Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Anyone who looks for omens,
the omen comes to him,
phrases.notes: He means the omen turns against him and harms him.

phrases.english: as it says: "For there is no omen in Jacob."
phrases.notes: במדבר 23:23. רבי reads לא here as if it were לו, 'to him'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי כֹּל הַמְנַחֵשׁ לוֹ נַחַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the flip side: being תמים brings good, while chasing omens, like chasing stars, brings harm.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever looks for omens is harmed by omens.

steps.title: But the word in the verse is spelled 'no', not 'to him'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי's reading: the פסוק spells לא with ל and א, which means 'no', not לו, 'to him'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written with a ל and an א!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי's proof. The spelling in the פסוק does not fit his reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's proof works only if the word means 'to him' (לו). But the פסוק actually says לא, 'there is no omen in Jacob.' So the פסוק cannot be the source for his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, used to open a challenge
It is written
The letters ל and א, spelling לא, 'no'

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not throwing out רבי's rule that the omen-seeker gets hurt. It only rejects the פסוק as his proof.

phrases.english: But it is written with a lamed and an alef!
phrases.notes: Spelled this way, the word means 'no', not לו, 'to him'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק that רבי just used.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's reading of 'כי לא נחש' as 'לו נחש'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The written spelling is לא, which means 'no' and does not mean 'to him', so the פסוק does not support the rule.

steps.title: The real reason is measure for measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the omen-seeker is harmed because of מדה כנגד מדה, and not because of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because of measure for measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps רבי's rule but gives it a new reason. The reason is מדה כנגד מדה, and the פסוק is not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק cannot be read as 'to him', the rule needs a different basis. A person who puts his trust in omens is paid back in the same way: the omens themselves come against him.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, introduces a corrected explanation
Measure for measure: a person is paid back in the same way he acts

steps.whatToRemember: Being תמים with הקדוש ברוך הוא brings success and ה׳'s matching wholeheartedness. Chasing stars or omens brings harm, מדה כנגד מדה. Israel is not ruled by the stars.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because of measure for measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by moving the rule from a פסוק to a principle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the source: the rule stays, but its basis moves from the פסוק to the principle of מדה כנגד מדה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The harm to the omen-seeker was learned from reading 'לא' as 'לו' in the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The harm comes from מדה כנגד מדה; the פסוק really says 'there is no omen in Jacob.'

steps.title: Someone who avoids omens is brought closer than the angels
steps.stepSummary: אהבה בריה דרבי זירא teaches that a person who does not use omens is brought into an inner place that even the angels cannot enter.
steps.simpleTranslation: אהבה, the son of רבי זירא, taught: Any person who does not look for omens is brought into a special inner area that even the ministering angels cannot enter. The פסוק says: 'For there is no divination in יעקב and no sorcery in ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the good side of the omen discussion. A person who does NOT chase omens gets a great reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, in steps 17-19, we learned that a person who looks for omens is harmed by them. Now we learn the opposite: a person who trusts ה׳ without omens is brought very close to Him, even closer than the angels.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who looks for omens or signs to predict what will happen
A partition. Here it means a special inner place near ה׳
The ministering angels
Sorcery or fortune-telling

phrases.english: Ahava, son of Rabbi Zeira, taught:
Any person who does not use omens,
is brought into a partitioned area
that even the ministering angels
cannot enter inside it,
as it is stated: "For there is no divination in Jacob
phrases.notes: במדבר 23:23. The rest of the פסוק says ישראל is told what ה׳ does, which shows how close they are to Him.

phrases.english: and no sorcery in Israel, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the positive flip side of רבי's teaching that omen-seekers are harmed by omens.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who does not look for omens is brought into a place closer to ה׳ than the angels.

steps.title: אברהם was punished for drafting Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו quoting רבי אלעזר says that אברהם was punished, and his children were enslaved in מצרים for 210 years, because he drafted תלמידי חכמים into war.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי אלעזר: Why was אברהם אבינו punished, so that his children were slaves in מצרים for 210 years? Because he forced תלמידי חכמים into service, as the פסוק says: 'He led forth his trained men, born in his house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: what did אברהם do wrong that caused the slavery in מצרים? This is the first of three answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads 'his trained men' as אברהם's students, who were תלמידי חכמים. Taking them away from Torah to fight a war was treated like a forced draft, and that is the sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Was punished
Were enslaved
Forced labor or a forced draft, like a king forcing people to work for him
His trained men, read here as his students

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Elazar said:
For what reason was Abraham our father punished
and his children enslaved to Egypt
for two hundred and ten years?
Because he made a forced draft of Torah scholars,
phrases.notes: He took his students away from learning and made them go to war with him.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "He led forth his trained men,
phrases.notes: בראשית 14:14

phrases.english: born in his house."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new aggadic topic about אברהם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אברהם was punished for drafting תלמידי חכמים into war.

steps.title: שמואל: אברהם questioned ה׳'s promise
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says אברהם was punished because he went too far in questioning ה׳ when he asked, 'How shall I know that I will inherit it?'
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: It was because he went too far with the ways of הקדוש ברוך הוא, as the פסוק says: 'How shall I know that I will inherit it?'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second, different reason for אברהם's punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ promised אברהם the land, and אברהם asked for a sign. שמואל sees this as asking too much instead of simply trusting ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: Went too far, overstepped
His ways or attributes (ה׳'s)
I will inherit it

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Because he went too far

phrases.aramaic: עַל מִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: concerning the ways of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it is stated: "How shall I know that I will inherit it?"
phrases.notes: בראשית 15:8

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question asked in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אברהם was punished for asking ה׳ for a sign instead of trusting His promise.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: אברהם kept people from coming close to ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says אברהם was punished because he let the captives go back to the king of סדום instead of bringing them close to the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It was because he kept people from entering under the wings of the שכינה, as the פסוק says: 'Give me the people, and take the goods for yourself.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a third reason for אברהם's punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the war, the king of סדום asked for the people back. If אברהם had kept those people with him, he could have taught them to serve ה׳. By giving them back, he lost that chance.

keyTerms.meaning: Kept away, separated
The wings of the Divine Presence, meaning coming close to ה׳
The goods, the property

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up הִפְרִיז (שמואל, step 22: 'went too far') with הִפְרִישׁ (רבי יוחנן: 'kept away'). They sound alike but mean different things.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three opinions on why אברהם was punished: רבי אלעזר says he drafted תלמידי חכמים, שמואל says he questioned ה׳'s promise, and רבי יוחנן says he kept people from coming close to the שכינה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Because he kept people away
from entering under the wings of the Divine Presence,
as it is stated: "Give me the people,
phrases.notes: בראשית 14:21. The king of סדום said this, and אברהם let the people go back with him.

phrases.english: and take the goods for yourself."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: שֶׁהִפְרִישׁ בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אברהם was punished for keeping people from coming under the wings of the שכינה.

steps.title: What does the word ויריק mean?
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the פסוק from step 21, רב says אברהם filled his men with Torah, and שמואל says he showered them with gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the פסוק 'He led forth his trained men, born in his house': רב said it means he poured Torah into them. שמואל said it means he poured gold onto them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the פסוק quoted by רבי אלעזר and asks what the unusual word ויריק means. רב and שמואל each explain it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ויריק can mean 'he emptied out' or 'poured out'. רב says אברהם poured Torah into his students, which fits רבי אלעזר's view that they were תלמידי חכמים. שמואל says he poured gold onto them, meaning he paid them well so they would fight with him.

keyTerms.meaning: He poured out to them, he showered them
Gold

phrases.english: "He led forth his trained men, born in his house":
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק from step 21. Now the גמרא explains the word ויריק.

phrases.english: Rav said: He showered them with Torah.
And Shmuel said: He showered them with gold.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַיָּרֶק אֶת חֲנִיכָיו יְלִידֵי בֵיתוֹ״, רַב אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the פסוק cited in step 21 to explain one of its words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: ויריק means he filled them with Torah. שמואל: it means he gave them gold.

steps.title: אליעזר was worth all 318 men
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי בר אבא explains the 318 men of אברהם: אליעזר alone was equal to all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah says אברהם went to war with 'eighteen and three hundred' men. רבי אמי בר אבא said: אליעזר was equal to all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the same פסוק about the war of אברהם and focuses on the number 318. רבי אמי בר אבא says אליעזר by himself was as strong as all those men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading there really were 318 men, but אליעזר alone balanced all of them. It praises אליעזר, the servant of אברהם, as being as great as the whole group.

keyTerms.meaning: Eighteen and three hundred, meaning 318 men
The servant of אברהם
Equal to all of them

phrases.english: "Eighteen and three hundred"
phrases.notes: Still the same פסוק from step 21: בראשית 14:14, the men אברהם took to war.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami bar Abba said:
Eliezer was equal to all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי בַּר אַבָּא: אֱלִיעֶזֶר כְּנֶגֶד כּוּלָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק (בראשית 14:14) that steps 21 and 24 discussed, now focusing on the number 318.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אליעזר alone was equal in strength to all 318 men.

steps.title: The 318 was really just אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: A second version says the 318 refers to אליעזר alone, since the letters of his name add up to 318.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: it was only אליעזר, because the number value of his name is exactly this amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the teaching. Here the number 318 is a hint to one person, אליעזר, because his name adds up to 318.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25 there were 318 real men and אליעזר matched them all. Here there is only one man, and the number in the פסוק is a code for his name. So אברהם went to war with just אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Its number count, the number value of the letters

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In step 25 there were 318 men and אליעזר was worth all of them. In step 26 there were no 318 men at all, only אליעזר.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
It is Eliezer alone,
because his number comes out to this amount.
phrases.notes: Count it out: א 1, ל 30, י 10, ע 70, ז 7, ר 200. That adds up to 318.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֱלִיעֶזֶר הוּא, דְּחוּשְׁבָּנֵיהּ הָכִי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רבי אמי בר אבא's reading of the number 318.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 318 in the פסוק is the number value of אליעזר's name, so only אליעזר went with אברהם.

steps.title: אברהם recognized ה׳ at age three
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי בר אבא learns from the number value of עקב (172) that אברהם recognized his Creator at age three.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אמי בר אבא said: אברהם recognized his Creator when he was three years old, as it says, 'Because (עקב) אברהם listened to My voice.' The number value of עקב is 172.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי בר אבא gives another teaching that uses number values. The word עקב adds up to 172, which he reads as the number of years אברהם listened to ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם lived 175 years. If he listened to ה׳ for 172 of them, he must have started at age three. The word עקב, which simply means 'because', is read as a hint to the number of years.

keyTerms.meaning: Recognized his Creator
Because; its letters add up to 172
To My voice

steps.whatToRemember: Two teachings here use number values: אליעזר adds up to 318, and עקב adds up to 172. Since אברהם lived 175 years, he recognized ה׳ at age three.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ami bar Abba said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּן שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים הִכִּיר אַבְרָהָם אֶת בּוֹרְאוֹ,
phrases.english: At three years old, Abraham recognized his Creator,
as it is said:
"Because Abraham listened to My voice"
phrases.notes: בראשית 26:5

phrases.english: Its number is one hundred and seventy-two.
phrases.notes: ע 70, ק 100, ב 2 makes 172. אברהם lived 175 years, so he started at age three.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי בַּר אַבָּא: בֵּן שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים הִכִּיר אַבְרָהָם אֶת בּוֹרְאוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same רבי אמי בר אבא, again using number values, now about when אברהם first recognized ה׳.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אברהם recognized his Creator at age three, because עקב adds up to 172 and he lived 175 years.

steps.title: Opening a teaching of רמי בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a statement of רמי בר אבא, which continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רמי בר אבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up the next move. The גמרא is about to bring a teaching from רמי בר אבא, and his words come right after this.
